thread:
Marta: Heads up — after the kernel-selection merge yesterday we're seeing a noticeable latency regression on long-sequence workloads (>=2048). NL-large p95 +18%, p99 +32% vs baseline. Posting quick repro and logs. @Kevin @Ciara :eyes:

Marta: Repro command we used (smoketests):
```
./bench_harness --model nl-large --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kernels=auto --runs 50 --collect p50,p95,p99
```

Marta: Raw p99 samples attached in CI: http://ci.internal/bench/180123/ (compare run 1789 vs 1799)

BenchBot: Automated alert: kernel-selector v2.1 deployed at 1801200000 triggered latency anomaly on bench-suite/nl-large (p99 delta +30%). Links: <http://ci.internal/alerts/180123|details> :warning:

Kevin: Thanks. Did we switch the fused-attn fallback for that model? IIRC kernel-selector now prefers kernel_A for seq>1024 unless mem pressure.

Marta: Yes — selector now picks kernel_A by throughput heuristics for long sequences. Kernel_A has different loop reorder and uses tiled attention path. Works great on most nets but maybe regresses on this architecture.

Ciara: Can you paste the perf counters? specifically l2_miss, sm_eff, and kernel occupancy from the failing run. Also confirm quantization settings (we had a change to q8 folding last week).

Marta: Perf extract (trimmed):
```
run 1799: p99=240ms, p95=110ms
  kernel_A: l2_miss=12.4%, sm_eff=72%, occupancy=61%
  baseline (kernel_B): l2_miss=9.1%, sm_eff=81%, occupancy=67%
qconfig: q8_dynamic enabled
```

Raj: Hardware same as baseline? driver/ CUDA versions? Even small driver tweaks change occupancy behavior.

Marta: Same node pool (g5x2), CUDA 12.2, drivers unchanged. Verified by node tag.

Kevin: Interesting — kernel_A lower occupancy + higher L2 miss. Could be tiling causing bad memory stride for our attention layout at seq=4096. Two quick checks: 1) run kernel_A with prefetch turned off; 2) rerun with KV-cache warm path (we had a micro-change to KV caching in selector).

Ciara: Also run with continuous batching disabled (set --batching=off). Batching can amplify strided access patterns for long sequences.

Marta: Will run three variants and paste results in ~30m. Quick note: the harness aggregates across microshards; we should isolate single-stream to avoid scheduling noise. Using `--batch 1 --single-stream` for the followups.

BenchBot: New job queued: http://ci.internal/bench/job/180123-run2 (params: kernel_A/no-prefetch, kernel_A/kv-warmoff, kernel_A/batching-off). Estimated finish ~20m.

Kevin: If we confirm kernel_A is worse, two paths: revert selector rule for seq>2048, or teach kernel_A a new memory-tiling heuristic. Revert is low risk but loses perf in other cases.

Ciara: For triage checklist — add correctness check: compare logits and softmax-norm between kernel_A and kernel_B on a handful of seeds. Not likely a numerical bug, but helps rule out silent correctness shifts. Also add p50/p95/p99 breakdown across token-position buckets (first 512, 512-2048, >2048).

Marta: Agreed. I'll include softmax diff and per-position histograms. Also will run a tiny eval set to check generation quality (v0.9 small prompt set).

Raj: If it's memory stride, could be a GPU-specific microcode edge. Capture Nsight timeline for 1 trace so we can see memory pattern. I'll help with that.

Marta: Results pasted from run2 (summary):
```
kernel_A / no-prefetch: p99=238ms (baseline 181), l2_miss=12.1%
kernel_A / kv-warmoff: p99=242ms, l2_miss=11.9%
kernel_A / batching-off: p99=190ms, l2_miss=9.5% \nbaseline (kernel_B): p99=182ms, l2_miss=9.0%
softmax-diff max=1.2e-6 (within atol)
per-pos: first512 p99 delta +2%, 512-2048 +10%, >2048 +42%
```

Ciara: That points strongly to batching interaction. Kernel_A seems sensitive to how multiple sequences are interleaved in memory.

Kevin: OK. Short-term: revert selector rule for sequences >2048 to prefer kernel_B. Long term: add a selector feature that simulates batch interleaving penalty (cheap heuristic using occupancy & l2_miss estimate).

Marta: Filing RFC follow-up and revert PR now. Revert PR will be small: change selector condition and add a canary flag. I'll link PR when created. :thumbsup:

BenchBot: PR created: http://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/5923 (revert kernel_A default for seq>2048). CI triggered.

Raj: After revert, let's schedule a canary rollout with 5% traffic and p99 guardrails for 48h. Also add a nightly e2e run that covers seq 4096 across both kernels.

Kevin: Adding selector telemetry: we should emit chosen_kernel + estimated_cost + observed_p99 for post-hoc tuning. Put it behind a debug flag for now.

Marta: Will do both: canary + telemetry. Thanks all. I'll ping when PR merges and when canary starts.

Ciara: Nice triage. Assign followups: Marta (PR+telemetry), Kevin (selector heuristic design doc), Raj (trace capture + canary plan).

Marta: Assigned. Back to running final QA. :coffee:

BenchBot: Canary schedule created: canary-5pct-48h starting 1801240000. Monitoring alarms set for p99 > baseline*1.15.
